name: Slack Guard
description:
Slack Guard is a governance-first RailCall module for Slack workspaces: agents get visibility immediately, while every risky change is previewed, approved by a human, executed, and receipted before it touches your workspace.

This is v0.1.0, the connectivity milestone. slack.get_team_info (read) is live now - a successful call proves the bot token is valid and the handler reaches the real Slack Web API end to end, with a signed receipt. The module is being built out command-by-command from here against the plan below, in build order; CHANGELOG.md records exactly what is live in each version.

Planned command set (31 commands across 3 risk tiers):
Tier 1, read, execute immediately: get_team_info (LIVE), list_users, get_user_info, list_channels, get_channel_info, list_channel_members, get_channel_history, get_thread_replies, list_usergroups, list_files, get_dnd_status.
Tier 2, low-risk write, executed with a receipt: post_message, post_ephemeral, add_reaction, remove_reaction, add_pin, remove_pin, add_bookmark, edit_bookmark, remove_bookmark, add_reminder, complete_reminder, set_channel_topic, set_channel_purpose, create_channel, join_channel, schedule_message, cancel_scheduled_message.
Tier 3, high-risk write, requires the human approval airlock: rename_channel, archive_channel, unarchive_channel, delete_message, kick_user_from_channel, invite_to_channel, delete_file, update_usergroup_members, share_file_publicly, uninstall_app / revoke_token (break-glass, last).

Three governance presets ship with the module: Observer (every write, Tier 2 included, requires approval - the recommended default for a first install), Team Copilot (the tiered split above once Tier 2/3 land - reads free, low-risk writes receipted, high-risk writes airlocked), Open Community Hardened (Team Copilot, plus channel-membership and usergroup-membership changes hard-blocked rather than merely airlocked, and file public-sharing disabled outright - for large open/public workspaces where the abuse surface is worse than in a closed team).

Slack Guard resolves credentials only through RailCall's vault helper, uses certifi-backed verified HTTPS, never invokes curl or another subprocess, actively redacts credentials from every error, and never automatically retries a write with an uncertain outcome. Slack's Web API always returns HTTP 200 and signals failure through an {"ok": false, "error": "<code>"} body instead of an HTTP status code; the handler treats that as the primary, definitive failure signal.

Quick start: create a custom Slack app at api.slack.com/apps in your own workspace, add the bot scopes each command needs, install the app to your workspace, copy the Bot User OAuth Token (xoxb-...), save it as SLACK_BOT_TOKEN on the muhammad-akif-janjua-slack-guard::slack card in RailCall Studio -> Integrations, reload Modules, then run slack.get_team_info.

Example call: slack.get_team_info {}.

Limitations: scoped to a single-workspace custom-app bot token, the no-review install path - admin.* endpoints (org-wide user/audit/policy control) require an Enterprise Grid org-level install and are out of scope. Built for the RailCall Track A module contest.

contest:2026Q3

Zero model-provider destinations in the signed manifest. Slack Web API traffic is the only business integration path, not an LLM call; the handler never invokes a model-provider SDK or RailCall model-completion primitive.
